thread:
Ava (VP Eng): ok team, quick Q&A after the roadmap — focus is runtime perf, batching/caching, kernel tradeoffs. Drop short bullets and we'll follow up in threads.

Devon (Staff ML Eng): two quick things: 1) are we prioritizing latency vs cost for PLG customers? 2) any ETA on the quantized-kernel landing?

Ava (VP Eng): Good q. PLG gets latency-first defaults but with easy toggles for cost (batching/quant profiles). Dedicated customers get tailored SLOs. Quant kernel ETA: Priya?

Priya (Runtime Lead): planning: prototype quant kernels end of Q2, wide rollout after internal perf sign-off mid-Q3. Primary blockers: end-to-end perf regressions on short-context bursts.

Marco (Kernel Engineer): to unpack that — quant helps throughput but can increase per-token latency on short sequences because some ops move off fused paths. We're exploring a hybrid path: per-model kernel selection at runtime.

Jamie (Product PM): can you give an example of hybrid selection rules? so PM can write docs.

Marco (Kernel Engineer): example rule: if seq_len <= 64 && batch_size <= 8 => use low-latency fused kernel; else if batch_size >= 32 or using int8 => use quantized throughput kernel. We can encode as a simple policy: "latency_threshold_ms" and "throughput_pref".

Devon (Staff ML Eng): sounds good. How does KV cache interact? caching reduces tokens but increases memory. Any guidance?

Priya (Runtime Lead): KV caching default: enabled for chat routes, smart TTLs per conversation. Memory pressure fallback: we evict oldest prefixes + fall back to recompute if needed. We'll release a knob in console for per-route cache budget.

Liam (SRE): one ops note — evictions currently spike OOM alerts in staging when many long chats hit quantized instances. We should add a graceful degradation: route to a non-quant instance before OOM.

Priya (Runtime Lead): agreed — routing policy change is on my board. Plan: add "oom_grace_route" with cool-down to avoid thrash.

Ava (VP Eng): leadership ask: what's the risk of switching PLG default to hybrid-selection now? pros/cons?

Marco (Kernel Engineer): pro: better tail latency for small requests; con: adds complexity in kernel matrix and testing surface. Need robust perf harness to catch regressions.

Devon (Staff ML Eng): also regressions could be model-specific — some HF ops cause fallback. We need model-level flags during rollout.

Jamie (Product PM): action for product: we'll update docs and add a toggle in console labeled "Hybrid kernel selection (experimental)". Can engineering provide a short blurb for the tooltip?

Priya (Runtime Lead): I'll draft the tooltip + FAQ. Will include expected perf profile, known limitations, and a link to the perf dashboard.

Liam (SRE): follow-up: can we get an alert that specifically calls out WHEN routing moves traffic off quantized nodes? that would help triage.

Priya (Runtime Lead): yep — plan to emit a metric and event: routing_change{from, to, reason}. We'll wire it to ops channel.

Devon (Staff ML Eng): minor: can we expose per-route batching latency histograms to help tune batch windows? right now only global histos exist.

Marco (Kernel Engineer): that'll help — we can add per-route bucketing in runtime, low lift but needs storage. Priya, ok to prioritize after routing metrics?

Priya (Runtime Lead): yes. Routing metrics > per-route histos > UI surfaces.

Ava (VP Eng): sounds like clear priority stack. quick check: any blockers that need leadership help (hiring, infra credits, partner access)?

Marco (Kernel Engineer): hiring: one senior kernel engineer for fused-path work; infra: need additional perf GPU hours for perf harness (rough estimate: 6 weeks).

Ava (VP Eng): noted. I'll push for budget. Jamie, coordinate hiring request + infra ask with finance.

Jamie (Product PM): will do.

deploy-bot: Deployment queued: staging/runtime-hybrid-policy v0.3 -> staging (initiated by Priya).

Liam (SRE): quick ops tip: before we run large perf suites, run small synthetic smoke with high-concurrency to catch immediate OOM/eviction loops. Saved us last time.

Priya (Runtime Lead): agreed. I'll post a short checklist and the synthetic command in the eng-runtime channel.

Devon (Staff ML Eng): one last user-facing question: do we plan to change SDK defaults? if yes, what's visibility to customers?

Ava (VP Eng): we won't change SDK defaults without a deprecation cycle. For PLG defaults in cloud, we'll put an opt-in experimental flag, then 30-day notice for defaults change.

Priya (Runtime Lead): action items: 1) Marco: finalize hybrid selection prototype (ETA 2w). 2) Marco + Devon: run perf harness on 3 representative models (ETA 4w). 3) Priya: routing metrics + oom_grace_route (ETA 2w). 4) Jamie: docs + console toggle (ETA 3w). 5) Ava: budget/hiring follow-up. I'll file follow-up threads for each action.

Ava (VP Eng): thanks all — short and actionable. If anyone has a long write-up, drop it in #eng-runtime or ping me. :thumbsup:
